original_target.title: Uniqueness of the planar spin-glass ground-state pair

full_original_statement:
For each nearest-neighbor edge $`e`$ of $`\mathbb Z^2`$, sample $`J_e`$ independently from the standard Gaussian distribution. A spin configuration $`\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{\mathbb Z^2}`$ is a ground state if flipping any finite set of spins cannot decrease its energy; explicitly,

```math
\sum_{\{x,y\}\in\partial_E A}J_{\{x,y\}}\sigma_x\sigma_y\ge0
\quad\text{for every finite }A\subset\mathbb Z^2,
```

where $`\partial_E A`$ contains edges with exactly one endpoint in $`A`$. Is it almost surely true that the set of all ground states is exactly $`\{\sigma,-\sigma\}`$ for some $`\sigma`$? The assertion concerns all infinite-volume ground states, without restricting the boundary conditions used to construct them.

sources.scope_comparison: The target concerns all full-plane Gaussian infinite-volume ground states modulo sign, with arbitrary state construction. Itoi's unchanged title/abstract claims uniqueness in all dimensions, but the latest primary version's appended erratum explicitly restricts the theorem to a finite lattice, removes the L→infinity limit from Eq8, says infinite-volume convergence was assumed in the proof and is not rigorously proved, and leaves RSB unresolved. Thus this is an older claim with acknowledged gap, not a complete matching announcement. Dario–Harel–Peled's2024primary Sections2.3.2/9 retain the full-plane conjecture and prove restricted translation-covariant results. No later repaired full proof was located.
